screens.title: Add policy: choose Allowlist
screens.spec: Add policy lists Allowlist with “Only addresses on your list can receive funds. Everything else is blocked.”
notes: Allowlist tile copy: “Transfer only tokens you pick to recipients you trust.” (from the protected Safe account banner)

screens.title: Allowlist intro
screens.spec: After picking Allowlist, explain what it does and that everything else is blocked before setup starts.
notes: From the edit-panels prototype (#9420): preview, three explainers, and “Every other action · Blocked” with an “I understand…” checkbox that unlocks Set up allowlist

screens.title: Pick the Safe account
screens.spec: The picker only lists Safe accounts where you're a signer or proposer.
notes: Lists only Safe accounts where the wallet is a signer or proposer, as in production
Accounts that can't have an allowlist stay in the list, greyed out, with the reason on hover (1.7, 1.8)
When no account is available, the dropdown says why (1.9, 1.10)

screens.title: Safe account needs an update
screens.spec: Older than 1.5.0: setup stops and offers the update.

screens.title: Another guard is installed
screens.spec: Setup stops when an unknown guard is already installed.
notes: Q6 is still open: what to do with an existing guard such as CoW Swap's

screens.title: Account already has an allowlist
screens.spec: One allowlist per Safe account, so setup sends you to edit the existing one.

screens.title: Network not supported
screens.spec: Only Ethereum, Polygon and Sepolia. Other networks don't offer setup and say why.
notes: Arbitrum and Base rows are greyed out. Hover one for: “Allowlists are only available on Ethereum, Polygon and Sepolia for now.”

screens.title: Nested Safe not supported
screens.spec: No nested Safes in this iteration (backlog 16.1).
notes: Grants is greyed out. Hover it for: “Allowlists aren't available yet for Safe accounts that have another Safe account as a signer.”

screens.title: No Safe account where the wallet is a signer
screens.spec: The wallet isn't a signer or proposer on any Safe account, so there's nothing to pick. Say why and offer to switch wallet.
notes: Production's message and Switch wallet button, unchanged

screens.title: No wallet connected
screens.spec: No wallet is connected, so the list can't be filtered by signer. Offer to connect one.
notes: Production's message and Connect wallet button, unchanged

screens.title: Tokens and recipients
screens.spec: Once the Safe has no open approvals, pick tokens (including ones it doesn't hold) and recipients.
notes: Prototype 3's search pickers, shown only after the approvals check passes
The edit flow still uses the old token and recipient lists

screens.title: Over the rule limit
screens.spec: Max 100 rules per transaction, 1,023 recipients per token, and it must fit one transaction's gas.
notes: Skipped for now, agreed with engineering

screens.title: Open approvals
screens.spec: Right after the Safe is picked, list its open approvals. They have to be revoked (on revoke.cash) before tokens and recipients can be chosen.
notes: Moved right after Safe selection, agreed with engineering
Not designed yet: loading while checking, and “we couldn't confirm the list is complete”

screens.title: Existing spending limits
screens.spec: Setup warns about the conflict and explains the outcome.
notes: No separate page any more: in the token list, tokens the Safe has spending limits for come first under “In spending limits”
Each has an info icon: “This Safe account has a spending limit for this token. Add the token, so the allowlist doesn't block the spending limit.”
Leave one of those tokens out and a yellow warning shows under the chips: “1 spending limit will be blocked by this allowlist.” (copy from #9420)
Open the token search on Treasury to see it
Documentation link (9.1.1) not added yet

screens.title: Safe account settings step
screens.spec: Not in M1: the first setup only creates token, ETH, MultiSend and deny-everything-else rules.
notes: Removed from the flow: setup goes Create, Review, Confirm, Execute

screens.title: “Everything else is blocked” confirmation
screens.spec: Setup states the Safe blocks every other action, and the user confirms before signing. If modules exist (like recovery), say the allowlist blocks them too.
notes: One red warning at the top of Review: what the Safe account can send, with the confirmation checkbox inside it
Continue scrolls back to the checkbox until it's ticked
Marked done without the module line (4.5.1)

screens.title: Review
screens.spec: What the Safe account will be able to send, and the setup transaction.
notes: One warning at the top, with the confirmation in it (see 2.6); the header banner is hidden on this step
“Every other action · Blocked” is the last row of the summary, its badge lined up with the other values
“Allowed account changes” removed, along with the settings step

screens.title: Confirm and execute
screens.spec: Collect signatures, then execute. Safe Shield checks on the right.

screens.title: Processing
screens.spec: After executing, don't offer Finish until the CGW serves the change. Then the table shows the new status.
notes: The row shows the grey “Processing” tag with a spinner until the change shows up, then moves to its new status
Hover the tag for what it's waiting for
Not designed: holding back Finish in the setup flow until the change shows up

screens.title: Allowlist is now active
screens.spec: Confirms once that the Safe only sends allowed tokens to allowed recipients, and that changes take 24 hours.

screens.title: Off-chain signatures stop working
screens.spec: Setup swaps the fallback handler, so the Safe can't confirm off-chain signatures any more.
notes: Spec only asks for documentation (11.8). Confirm whether setup should also say it

screens.title: Row content
screens.spec: Name with recipient count, first three token icons plus a count (hover lists all), Safe name with copy and link, status with a tooltip saying what it waits for.
notes: Columns: Policy, Safe account, Network, Details, Status
Policy name only: the line under it is gone
New Details column, built with the design system's AvatarGroup (24px): allowlists show token logos and recipient initials, first three then +n; hover lists them all
Spending limits show the token and the spender's initials; proposers show the proposer's initials
Status tooltips say what the policy waits for (signatures, execution or when it applies)
Not yet: copy button and link next to the Safe name (5.1.4)

screens.title: Filter by allowlist
screens.spec: Filter for recipient allowlists.
notes: The Workspace queue's toolbar, copied from production: Search, Group by, Filter and New
Filter has a submenu each for Status, Policy type, Safe account and Network, with a count next to every option
Picked filters show as chips under the toolbar (“Status: Ready to execute or apply”), with Clear
Group by: Urgency (one list, the default), Policy type, Safe account or Network. Click a group to collapse it; the header has collapse all
Groups that need action come first

screens.title: Search and empty state
screens.spec: Search by Safe, address, token, network and recipient, with an empty state.

screens.title: Default sort
screens.spec: Sort by status by default, rows that need action first.
notes: Rows that need someone to act come first: blue “ready” tags, then yellow ones waiting for signatures
Then blocked and failed, then expired, then rows waiting out the delay or processing, then active ones

screens.title: Status labels and colours
screens.spec: “Setup pending · n/m”, “Setup ready to execute”, “Processing”, “Edit in delay”, “Edit ready to apply”, “Edit expired”, “Removal …”, “Guard removal …”. Yellow waiting, blue ready, green active, grey expired.
notes: Every tag from the spec, in the product's badge colours: yellow waiting, blue ready, green active, grey expired
The table has one example row for every tag, on the Ethereum Safes (Payments and Treasury). Those example rows don't open a side panel
The table uses them for allowlist rows; spending limits and proposers keep their current chips
Not in the spec, so to confirm: “Setup failed” (red) and the spinner on “Processing”
Spec 5.1.6 splits the change and its status into two columns; this shows them in one tag

columns.name: Side panel: setup pending and active

screens.title: Active
screens.spec: Name and status, recipients and tokens with expandable lists, Safe, network, last update and the guard with an explorer link.

screens.title: Setup waiting for signatures
screens.spec: What's in force now, signature count, and the action for each viewer: connect, review, copy link or execute.
notes: All viewer variants exist in the full prototype (no wallet, signed, not signed, not a signer, fully signed)

screens.title: Failed, replaced, deleted
screens.spec: Shows what happened to the transaction after it left the queue.
notes: Expired changes have their own panel (6.5)

screens.title: Not a signer
screens.spec: Non-signers get a disabled button with the reason.

screens.title: Guard no longer installed
screens.spec: If the guard was removed outside the flow, say the allowlist isn't applied.
notes: Red “Not applied” tag and panel: its guard was removed outside Safe{Wallet}, so transactions aren't checked
Action: Remove allowlist

screens.title: Edit and review changes
screens.spec: Add or remove tokens and recipients. Review marks each one Added or Removed.

screens.title: Change request waiting for signatures
screens.spec: Same as setup, labelled “Edit pending · n/m”, with the current rules still in force.
notes: Setup's panel with edit copy: what still applies, the signatures, Review transaction
Fully signed, every “ready to execute” banner turns blue and positive: “The change is almost ready. Execute the transaction to start the 24-hour wait.”

screens.title: Change request in review window
screens.spec: Requested date, applies-from date and expiry. Apply is disabled and shows the time left.
notes: Says when it applies, and that any signer can cancel before then
Action: Cancel change

screens.title: Change request ready to apply
screens.spec: After the delay, offer Apply and say nothing happens automatically. Show signatures needed and the deadline.
notes: Blue banner: the 24 hours are over, applying needs its own transaction, and it expires after 7 days
Actions: Apply change, Cancel change
“Apply pending” and “Apply ready to execute” reuse the signatures panel

screens.title: Change request expired
screens.spec: After 7 days the change expires. Current rules stay; offer to discard.
notes: Grey banner: it wasn't applied in time, so nothing changed
Action: Edit

screens.title: Active with a change waiting
screens.spec: How the table and panel show an active allowlist with a pending change. The spec asks design for this.
notes: Same panel as 6.3: when it applies, the review window dates, Apply disabled until then, Cancel change
Cancelling needs a signed transaction (S28–S31); non-signers get the buttons disabled with the reason

screens.title: Cancel a change request or removal
screens.spec: Cancel during the delay with a signed transaction. Current rules stay.
notes: “Cancel pending” and “Cancel ready to execute” use the signatures panel
Q8 still open: is cancelling in Milestone 1?

screens.title: Removal waiting for signatures
screens.spec: Recipients and tokens shown as removed. The allowlist stays active until the removal applies.

screens.title: Removal in review window, ready, expired
screens.spec: Same delay, apply and expiry steps as an edit.
notes: Same stages as edit, with removal copy; the lists read as removed until it’s cancelled or expires
Open the other removal stages from the “Side panels · spec 5.7 states” row of All states

screens.title: Guard removal
screens.spec: After the rules are removed the guard still blocks everything. Say the Safe can't send anything and offer to remove the guard.
notes: Merged into removal: removing the allowlist is one change with the 24-hour review window, so there’s no separate step

screens.title: Removal pending in the table
screens.spec: The table shows removal as pending until the last transaction executes.
notes: Every removal stage has its tag in the table (see 4.5)

screens.title: Safe Shield on transfers
screens.spec: Before signing a transfer, Safe Shield says whether the allowlist allows this recipient and token.
notes: From the engineering allowlist demo: “Policy checks passed” first in Safe Shield's Pro checks, or “This account's policies will refuse this transaction.” in red
Storybook: Allowlist MVP · Safe Shield on transfers
On a refusal the header turns red: “Blocked by policy”

screens.title: New spending limit with an allowlist
screens.spec: The spending limit flow warns about the conflict.
notes: Tokens outside the allowlist are disabled with a tooltip
Add the documentation link (9.2.1)

screens.title: Spending limit blocked by the allowlist
screens.spec: The spending limit panel says the allowlist blocks it.
